value.rationale: The repaired physical question is when a stable coexistence state appears and disappears as fear increases in an explicit family outside the earlier sufficient two-root regime. The interval is motivated by two local dynamical thresholds, not arbitrarily chosen parameter digits: at its lower endpoint the boundary's critical quadratic drift vanishes, while its upper endpoint is the loss of transverse hyperbolicity of the other boundary state. Selecting the physical branch and finding exact width explains how the coexistence window closes and makes the distinction between coexistence as an attractor and as a saddle explicit. This remains useful without a general boundary coefficient priority claim.
residual_risks: The contribution is a model-specific, readily computable phase boundary. It does not generalize the qualitative saddle-node–transcritical mechanism, assert global basins, or give experimentally calibrated coefficients.
